A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POATE attack and CoT defenses. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack and defense experiments, model-size comparisons, template analyses and human-versus-generated prompt evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, broader defense evaluations, few-shot sensitivity results and harmfulness-evaluator analyses.

M1.justification: The attack stages and both CoT defense prompts are retained. However, new Algorithm 1 returns the first prompt when both attempts fail, while Section 3.2 in both versions says the second-stage output is taken as-is. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a changed fallback or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate harmful queries from AdvBench, XSTest and MaliciousInstructions with the same category coverage. The added experiments reuse these datasets and tasks; additional model configurations do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds ArtPrompt and Fallacy Failure Attack (FFA) to the attack comparison in Table 1 and evaluates both under the proposed defenses in new Table 13. Existing attack comparators and the seven defense baselines are retained. FFA materially strengthens the comparison, matching POATE's average GPT-4o ASR.

E3.justification: Table 3 expands defense evaluation from Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B to include Llama-2-7B, Phi-3-mini and GPT-4o. New experiments compare eight versus 32 few-shot examples, with differing intent annotations, and apply a 1–5 harmfulness metric to GPT-4o responses. The original 50 queries per dataset, binary ASR procedure and generation settings remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds a sensitivity study testing how demonstration count and explicit intent annotations affect polar-opposite generation (Table 7). Appendix A.7 and Figures 11–13 add an analysis of harmfulness-judge failures on mixed safe/unsafe responses. Earlier template, scaling, intent-shift and human-written-prompt analyses are retained, including material moved into Appendix D.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6 retains seed 42, and neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Human/GPT-4 agreement reporting is unchanged, moving from v1 Table 9 to v3 Table 11.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 rows and overlapping defense results are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial result entries. FFA and POATE both average 72.67% ASR on GPT-4o, revising the best-baseline comparison without changing POATE's scores. New results also include defenses on three additional models, XSTest intention-shift rates of 40%, 32% and 22%, and harmfulness means of 1.55, 1.56 and 1.47.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The polar-opposite concept is substantively unchanged; the added pseudocode and empirical harmfulness scale do not introduce mathematical theory or derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the approximately 98% defense reduction reported across two models with approximately 93% and 95% reductions for the two defenses across five models, and drops the stated 64% advantage over SmoothLLM. The central POATE, model-size vulnerability and CoT-defense contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly argues that the 1–5 harmfulness judge underestimates responses combining safe and unsafe information, qualifying that metric's applicability and explaining the retained binary evaluation approach. Existing limitations concerning intent shifts, single-turn attacks and untested Claude/Gemini models remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds Algorithm 1, ArtPrompt/FFA implementation descriptions and prompt examples, and explanations for missing GPT-4o defense results. The published code link changes to a differently named repository. Existing hardware, runtimes, generation parameters and 32-example prompt sets are retained; repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2024) and explicitly positions Reverse Thinking CoT as an adaptation of that reasoning approach. It also adds the Mistral 7B citation. The duplicate Puzzler references are consolidated without removing a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract and portions of the introduction and results are rewritten, particularly to foreground both defenses. Main-text error analysis and Appendix C.3 are regrouped into Appendix D, with the defense appendix becoming E. Most methodological, related-work and limitations prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a full-width algorithm, three tables and five baseline-prompt or evaluator-error figures. Table 1 gains comparator rows, and Table 3 changes from vertically stacked model blocks to a full-width five-model comparison. Generation prompts and the human-versus-POATE chart move to the appendices; existing bar-chart content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens comparative validity and support for defense generality: it evaluates the closely related FFA attack, acknowledges its GPT-4o tie, and extends defense evidence beyond two selected open models. The few-shot study and evaluator-error analysis also make design choices and measurement limitations more assessable. These gains outweigh the localized fallback ambiguity in Algorithm 1 and remaining stale two-model wording in Section 5.
